header.title: How to Repair a Chest Freezer that Leaks
header.description: This guide provides instructions on how to address a leaking chest freezer by focusing on clearing a blocked drain tube and initiating a defrost cycle.

steps.description: This step instructs you to locate and inspect the freezer's drain tube to identify potential blockages causing a leak.
actions: Locate the drain tube at the back of the freezer.
Remove the back panel if necessary to access the drain tube.
Rub the tube to check if it feels tight or bloated.

steps.description: Use a straightened wire hanger to attempt to clear a potential clog from the drain tube.
actions: Straighten a wire hanger.
Push the wire up the tube.
Check for resistance.
Poke the clog out of the tube (if possible).
Place a drain pan under the tube.

steps.description: Empty the freezer, check for a blocked drain hole, and clear the blockage with a wire hanger.
actions: Unplug the chest freezer
Remove all the food inside
Store food in the bath with a towel
Move easily defrosting items to another freezer
Check for a blocked drain hole
Locate the drain hole at the bottom
Push through the drain hole with a wire hanger
Remove as much of the clog as possible

steps.description: Defrost the freezer completely, taking precautions to preserve frozen food and monitor for leaks afterward.
actions: Store frozen food in other freezers or cook it.
Allow the freezer to defrost completely for 24 hours.
Empty the drain pan a couple of times.
Wipe out the inside of the chest freezer.
Ensure there’s a small, clear area around the drain hole.
Plug the freezer back in.
Allow the freezer to cool properly.
Keep checking for leaks from the chest freezer.
